transcript.text: Today we will look at Python functions.
Let's say we have a function called greet. We pass it a name, and it prints hello. For example, greet('mary') prints hello mary.
The parameter here is just a placeholder. It could be called anything.
Now let us look at return values. A function can return a result instead of just printing.
Using return, the function sends a value back to the caller. This is more flexible than print.
You can assign the returned value to a variable and use it later.
Default parameters let you define a fallback value. If the caller does not pass an argument, the default is used.
Keyword arguments allow you to pass values by name rather than position, making calls more readable.
Scope is about where a variable is visible. Variables inside a function are local by default.
The global keyword lets a function modify a variable defined outside. Use it sparingly.
Lambda expressions create small anonymous functions inline, useful for short callbacks.
That covers the basics of functions in Python. Practice by writing your own.
